mariadb.defaultConnection.markdownDescription: The connection URI new SQL editors run on, as listed by `db.list_connections`. Set it from the context menu of a connection in the **Connections** view.

mariadb.actions.logAllCalls.markdownDescription: Log every MCP call in the MariaDB panel's Actions, not only what was done. Calls made on an open connection - browsing its schemas and objects - are added to that connection's Actions. Those made on no open connection - listing the connections, and adding, editing, moving, deleting and testing them - are shown under **General Actions** in the panel's connection picker. A call that fails is logged either way.

enumDescriptions: Opening a connection in the Connections view connects it.
A connection is only opened by the Connect button or command.
mariadb.connections.connectMode.markdownDescription: How a connection in the **Connections** view is opened. `onOpen` connects as soon as the connection is expanded, and leaves the Connect button off the row; `explicit` keeps the button and never connects on its own.

mariadb.overview.showOnStartup.markdownDescription: Open the **MariaDB Overview** editor tab - a tile per connection, to open a SQL editor on - the first time the **Connections** view is shown in a window. It can always be opened from the view's toolbar or with **MariaDB: Show MariaDB Overview**.

mariadb.overview.showGreeting.markdownDescription: Show the welcome text above the connection tiles of the **MariaDB Overview**. Closing it there turns this off.

mariadb.execute.stopOnError.markdownDescription: Whether a failing statement ends the script. Turn this off to run every statement and collect all the failures, which suits a script of independent statements. A single file can be switched from the editor's toolbar without changing this; it starts out doing whatever this says.

mariadb.execute.pageSize.markdownDescription: How many rows of a result set are fetched and shown at a time. A `SELECT` without a `LIMIT` of its own is given one, and the result set's toolbar pages through the rest.

enumDescriptions: As the SQL file's connection's sql_mode says, once the connection is open.
Always an identifier, as under ANSI_QUOTES.
Always a string, as in the default sql_mode.
mariadb.sql.ansiQuotes.markdownDescription: Whether `"..."` in a SQL file is highlighted as a string or as an identifier, as the server reads it under `ANSI_QUOTES`. The identifier colouring is a semantic highlight, so it shows only where `#editor.semanticHighlighting.enabled#` is on - which the built-in themes turn on.

mariadb.lsp.enabled.markdownDescription: Whether SQL files get diagnostics, completion, hover, outline and the other language features of the MariaDB SQL language server, `mariadb-lsp`. It is looked for in `#mariadb.lsp.path#`, else on the PATH, else next to `mariadb-shell` in the MariaDB Shell's installation.

mariadb.lsp.path.markdownDescription: The `mariadb-lsp` executable to use. Empty: the first on the PATH, else the one next to `mariadb-shell` in the MariaDB Shell's installation (`~/.local/share/mariadb-shell/<version>/bin`, or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\mariadb-shell\<version>\bin` on Windows).

mariadb.lsp.threads.markdownDescription: How many threads the language server checks statements with. 0: one per CPU core.

mariadb.lsp.catalogFiles.markdownDescription: SQL files whose schema objects every SQL file sees in completion, hover and go to definition, read in this order as one script. A directory stands for its `*.sql` files. Relative paths are from the first workspace folder. Saving one of them reads them again.

mariadb.lsp.catalogRefreshSeconds.markdownDescription: How often the language server reads a connection's tables, columns and routines again, in seconds. 0: when a file first uses the connection, and after a script with `CREATE`, `ALTER`, `DROP` or `RENAME` runs from an editor.

mariadb.lsp.keywordCase.markdownDescription: The case completion writes keywords and built-in functions in.

enumDescriptions: As the editor indents the file (`editor.insertSpaces`, `editor.tabSize`); the lines completion adds use a tab where the line has tabs, else two spaces.
mariadb.lsp.indentation.markdownDescription: One level of indentation in formatted queries and in the `FROM` and `JOIN` lines completion adds.

mariadb.lsp.lineWidth.markdownDescription: The line width in characters that formatted SQL and the `JOIN` clauses completion adds stay within: past it, or in a statement that spans lines already, each clause starts a line of its own (a `FROM` completion adds always does). 0: no limit.

mariadb.lsp.indentClauses.markdownDescription: Formatting puts the clauses of a query or DML statement (`FROM`, `WHERE`, `SET`, ...) one level deeper than its first line, and the `FROM` completion adds goes there too. Off: at the statement's level. Routine bodies follow `#mariadb.lsp.indentRoutineClauses#`.

mariadb.lsp.indentRoutineClauses.markdownDescription: The same as `#mariadb.lsp.indentClauses#`, for the statements in the body of a procedure, function, trigger or event.

mariadb.lsp.completionAddsTables.markdownDescription: Completing a column of a table the query does not have yet adds the table: a `FROM` on a line of its own, or a `JOIN` on a foreign key; and the schema's tables are offered to join. Off: the column only.

mariadb.lsp.sqlMode.markdownDescription: The `sql_mode` SQL files are checked in, for example `ANSI_QUOTES,STRICT_TRANS_TABLES`. A file on a connection is checked in that server's `sql_mode` instead, and `SET sql_mode` in the file is followed.

mariadb.lsp.serverVersion.markdownDescription: The server version versioned comments (`/*!100500 ... */`) are judged against, for example `11.4.2`. Empty: the version of the grammar the language server was built from. A file on a connection uses that server's version instead. Changing it restarts the language server.

mariadb.lsp.debounceMs.markdownDescription: How long, in milliseconds, typing has to pause before the statements it changed are checked.

mariadb.lsp.maxDiagnostics.markdownDescription: The most problems reported per SQL file.

mariadb.lsp.progressThresholdMB.markdownDescription: SQL files at least this large, in megabytes, show how far their check has got in the status bar.

mariadb.lsp.trace.server.markdownDescription: Logs the messages between VS Code and the language server to the **MariaDB SQL Language Server** output.

mariadb.resultSet.freezePrimaryKeyColumn.markdownDescription: Whether a result set's primary key columns are frozen: moved to the front of the grid and kept in place while the rest scrolls sideways. A result set can switch this for itself in its toolbar's action menu; each starts out doing what this says.

mariadb.resultSet.showColumnDataTypes.markdownDescription: Whether the result grid's header shows each column's data type in a smaller line under its name.

mariadb.keybindings.runScript.markdownDescription: The shortcut that runs the whole SQL file (or the selection). Any shortcut outside this list can be set in the Keyboard Shortcuts editor against `mariadb.runSqlFile`.

mariadb.keybindings.runStatementAtCursor.markdownDescription: The shortcut that runs only the statement the cursor is in. Any shortcut outside this list can be set in the Keyboard Shortcuts editor against `mariadb.runSqlStatement`.

mariadb.mrs.restDaemonUrl.markdownDescription: Where REST requests go for a server that no local REST Daemon serves; a tree row of a server with one, as the **REST Daemons** view lists them, uses that daemon instead. The **Open ... Request Path in Web Browser** commands and the client SDK's default service URL start with it.

mariadb.copilot.enabled.markdownDescription: Whether GitHub Copilot - and any other chat in VS Code - gets the MariaDB skills and the MariaDB Shell's MCP server. The server runs in agent mode: it opens only the connections that allow MCP access, and asks before it touches a path outside its allowed list. Starting it the first time installs the MariaDB Shell if there is none.
